To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TGF-ß-specific SMAD2/3/4 complex is involved in TGF-ß-activated gene expression through association with the histone methyltransferase complex MLL4.
the TGF-ß-specific SMAD proteins 2/3 are associated with the PTIP-MLL4 complex, which regulates TGFß-specific gene transcription.
PTIP and PAI1 are TGF-β specific SMAD interacting proteins, which link SMAD signaling to the MLL4 histone methyltransferase complex to regulate TGF-β-induced gene expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional role of the MLL4 subunit PTIP in relation to TFG-β-activated gene transcription.
the role of the histone methyltransferase MLL4 complex in TGF-β activated transcription.
the role of the MLL4 subunit PA1 and PTIIP in TGF-β-mediated gene transcription.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PA1 and PT1P are involved in SMAD-mediated TGF-β activated gene transcription.
PA1 and PTIF are involved in the TGF- signaling pathway, and the MLL4/PTIP/PA1 complex is required for the regulation of TGF--dependent transcriptional activation.
PA1 and PTIF are involved in TGF-β-mediated transcription regulation and that they are part of the MLL4 transcription complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MLL4/PA1/PTIP complex is a TGF-β activated complex that is involved in TGF-β specific transcription.
PTIP and PAI1 are involved in the regulation of TGF-beta signaling.
TGF-β specific SMADs interact with the MLL4 subunit PA1, which leads to a specific regulation of genes by the MLL complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that

TGF-β activated SMADs interact with the MLL4 histone H3 lysine 4 methyltransferase (KMT) complex to activate TGF-β target genes and that PA1 and PTIPI are novel proteins involved in TGF-β-mediated SMAD signaling.
TGF-β activated SMADs interact with the MLL4 histone methyltransferase complex, which is required for the transcriptional activation of TGF-β responsive genes.

PTIP is a novel SMAD3 interacting protein that regulates TGF-β-mediated gene transcription by the MLL methyltransferase complex, which has implications in the regulation of TGF-β-induced epithelial to mesenchymal transition.
